identity_ownership_footprint.value: U.S. system operates around a deeply embedded McDonald's-controlled restaurant platform (NEWPOS) and surrounding StoreTech ecosystem; McDonald's sold NEWPOS software to Capgemini, which remains deeply embedded.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: Core POS displacement is extremely unlikely without a major system mandate; any Genius motion must avoid sounding like platform replacement.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: PAR and NCR are the meaningful domestic hardware/POS infrastructure sources; field intelligence indicates dissatisfaction is strongest around NCR.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: Hardware dissatisfaction may create an entry point even when software-platform replacement does not.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: McDonald's global teams increasingly drive technology roadmap, architecture, data, and platform direction; this doesn't always translate cleanly to U.S. owner/operator reality.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: A global approval story alone will not move the U.S. system.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: McDonald's publicly announced Google Cloud restaurant connectivity and Edge, a Google-developed restaurant computing platform live in hundreds of U.S. restaurants and expanding globally.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: The Edge investment makes NEWPOS/platform displacement even less likely; DMB/hardware opportunities must prove Edge compatibility.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: McDonald's > NEXT was introduced at WWC as the next era of growth and productivity, with an ambition to be the customer's first choice every time and improve unit economics.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: NEXT favors wedges that reduce field friction and improve reliability, not broad re-platforming.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: Q2 2026: U.S. comparable sales slowed to roughly 0.8% while global comparable sales rose roughly 1.3%; management framed the U.S. miss as an execution problem, not a strategy problem.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: The Genius pitch should speak to execution reliability, supplier optionality, and field simplicity -- not challenge McDonald's strategy.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: Skye Anderson appointed president of McDonald's USA (previously U.S. COO), replacing Joe Erlinger.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: The U.S. decision map is changing; update the stakeholder map around U.S. operations and field reliability.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: NOA survey of 100+ operators (of ~2,000+ U.S. franchisees): 95% reported declining Q1 profitability; ~90% reported significantly negative cash flow vs. prior year; ~80% said cash flow is insufficient for required reinvestment obligations.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: Any technology wedge must compete on capital efficiency and lifecycle cost, not capability alone. Treat as franchisee-association-reported figures about a subset of the system, not McDonald's-corporate-confirmed.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: A new ~10-year remodel cycle is expected to begin 2027-2028; surveyed franchisees estimated per-store remodel cost of $400,000-$700,000 (a franchisee estimate, not a McDonald's-published number).
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: The remodel cycle is the buying event; franchisee cash-flow pressure changes the buying criteria toward capital efficiency.

identity_ownership_footprint.value: McDonald's "$3 and Under" menu plus Extra Value Meal discounts: three-quarters of franchisees said they were directly pressured into it; estimated $310 million in lost sales last quarter from discounts that didn't generate offsetting traffic.
identity_ownership_footprint.strategic_implication: Franchisee/operator validation matters more than ever -- McDonald's won't want another top-down rollout operators view as noise.
